q-37600.name: Question 1
q-37600.problem:
Consider the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}-3 & -8 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].$ You're given that ${\lambda }_{1}=-3$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=1$ are the eigenvalues of $A$, and
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$, ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ are the respective eigenvectors. Find the matrices $P$ and $D$ such that $PD{P}^{-1}=A,$ where $D$ is a diagonal matrix.
q-37600.worked_solution:
Since the eigenvalues of the matrix are ${\lambda }_{1}=-3$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=1,$ we construct the diagonal matrix $D$ by writing the eigenvalues in the main diagonal:

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, to construct the matrix $P,$ we simply write the respective eigenvectors as columns: 

- the $1$st column is the eigenvector corresponding to ${\lambda }_{1}=-3,$ and

- the $2$nd column is the eigenvector corresponding to ${\lambda }_{2}=1.$

Therefore, we get

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

D=[−3001].

q-37610.problem:
Consider the matrix $A$ for which ${\lambda }_{1}=3$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=15$ are eigenvalues, and

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

are the respective eigenvectors. What are the values of $a,b,c$ given that

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & b \\ 2 & c\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}a & 0 \\ 0 & 15\end{aligned}]{[\begin{aligned}1 & b \\ 2 & c\end{aligned}]}^{-1}?
$$
q-37610.worked_solution:
Since the eigenvalues of the matrix are ${\lambda }_{1}=3$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=15,$ we construct the diagonal matrix $D$ by writing the eigenvalues in the main diagonal:

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 15\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, to construct the matrix $P,$ we simply write the respective eigenvectors as columns: 

- the $1$st column is the eigenvector corresponding to ${\lambda }_{1}=3,$ and

- the $2$nd column is the eigenvector corresponding to ${\lambda }_{2}=15.$

Therefore, we get

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 15\end{aligned}]{[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}.
$$

 

In conclusion, we get $a=3,$ $b=-1,$ and $c=1.$

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}].

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}5 & -3 \\ 7 & 1\end{aligned}].

$$

Now, to construct the matrix P, we simply write the respective eigenvectors as columns:

q-80389.problem:
Consider the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 \\ -1 & 4\end{aligned}].$ You're given that ${\lambda }_{1}=3$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=6$ are the eigenvalues of $A$, and
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$, ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$ are the respective eigenvectors. Find the matrices $P$ and $D$ such that $PD{P}^{-1}=A,$ where $D$ is a diagonal matrix.
q-80389.worked_solution:
Since the eigenvalues of the matrix are ${\lambda }_{1}=3$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=6,$ we construct the diagonal matrix $D$ by writing the eigenvalues in the main diagonal:

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, to construct the matrix $P,$ we simply write the respective eigenvectors as columns: 

- the $1$st column is the eigenvector corresponding to ${\lambda }_{1}=3,$ and

- the $2$nd column is the eigenvector corresponding to ${\lambda }_{2}=6.$

Therefore, we get

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

a
D=[300−1] and P=[2131]
b
D=[−1003] and P=[2311]
c
D=[−1003] and P=[1213]
d
D=[−1003] and P=[2131]
e
D=[300−1] and P=[2311]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since the eigenvalues of the matrix are λ1=−1 and λ2=3, we construct the diagonal matrix D by writing the eigenvalues in the main diagonal:

D=[−1003].

Now, to construct the matrix P, we simply write the respective eigenvectors as columns:

  • the 1st column is the eigenvector corresponding to λ1=−1, and

  • the 2nd column is the eigenvector corresponding to λ2=3.

Therefore, we get

P=[2131].
